scenes.narration: The Titanic didn't sink because it hit an iceberg head-on. It sank because it didn't.
On April 14, 1912, the ship got several ice warnings from other ships, yet kept steaming at high speed through the night.
At 11:40 p.m., lookouts spotted an iceberg dead ahead. The crew turned hard, and the berg scraped along the starboard side.
Titanic could float with four front compartments flooded. The scrape opened up at least five.
The bulkheads didn't reach the top deck, so as the bow sank, water spilled over from one compartment into the next.
There were only twenty lifeboats, with room for about half the people on board. More than fifteen hundred died.
About two hours and forty minutes after the collision, it was gone. The iceberg made the hole, but the design decided how it ended.
